assessment.nobel_worthiness: Practical correction of spherical aberration in the TEM removed a limit that had stood since Scherzer's 1936 theorem, bringing sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms in materials, interfaces and defects into routine use. This is a new tool that opened a door to phenomena that could not be seen before, and it is an invention with a clear, verified outcome and very broad impact in physics, chemistry and materials science.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the multipole corrector design and theory, Haider and Urban built and demonstrated working correctors (TEM 1998, with Urban's group at Juelich), and the credited trio is a natural, compact configuration. Other contributors, notably Krivanek on the STEM corrector, are not in the supplied credit and would have to be weighed against the supplied three; I cannot independently verify the details of that dispute.
assessment.maturity: Correctors are installed worldwide and have been confirmed independently for over two decades; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the supplied credit omits Ondrej Krivanek, who developed the STEM corrector, and how the committee would treat the TEM and STEM branches.
Prize area fit (instrumentation versus discovery) may be questioned, though the invention clause applies directly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity at 26 K in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO opened an entirely new family of high-temperature superconductors with a new mechanism question and Tc values above 50 K soon afterwards. It is an original experimental discovery with lasting impact, rather than a later refinement.
assessment.attribution: Credit is clean: Hosono's group made the original observation, and the follow-up work by others (Chinese groups raising Tc) built directly on it. A single laureate is a plausible configuration; the earlier work on layered iron compounds by the same group is not in the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups within months and the field has matured for 18 years, but the pairing mechanism is still debated, and that does not diminish the discovery itself.
uncertainties: The mechanism of pairing remains unresolved, so the case rests on discovery rather than explanation.
Whether the committee would want additional laureates for the high-Tc follow-up discoveries is not settled by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reproducible room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions in 1995, followed by giant TMR in MgO junctions, gave the sensing basis for hard-disk read heads and magnetic random-access memory. This is a measured, experimental discovery with large technological benefit, building on the GMR prize of 2007.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995, an original and verified experiment; Parkin and Yuasa/Djayaprawira later achieved giant MgO TMR. Julliere's 1975 low-temperature observation predates all of these and is not credited, and the relation to the Nobel for GMR needs careful handling. Whether the MgO step should be credited to Parkin or to others (Yuasa, Butler, Mathon) is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Technologically deployed for nearly two decades and confirmed independently many times; timing is mature.
uncertainties: Julliere's priority and the MgO coherent-tunnelling contributors may complicate a clean credit.
Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may reduce the perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2013 observation of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies, and the later identification of a blazar and the Galactic plane as sources made it a verified, original experimental result and a new window on the universe. Instrument-building at the South Pole was a major achievement.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the project, and Karle was a decisive leader in the detector and the analysis, but IceCube is a large collaboration, and the committee would have to be certain that the people credited actually did the original work. The supplied two-name credit may omit important contributors to the first detection and to AMANDA.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation of the diffuse flux, plus source associations, is now accumulating; however, the origin of most of the flux is still uncertain, so timing is reasonable but not conclusive.
uncertainties: Attribution within a large collaboration is difficult; the supplied credited names may not capture all decisive roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, delivers fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and has become the basis for the redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. It is an invention of lasting value and clear measurement impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept (2001-2003) and Ye's group developed the strontium clock to record accuracy and coherence; this is a two-person configuration that is easy to defend, although ion-clock groups (NIST) and Hall/Haensch precedents are separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed by several independent laboratories; the redefinition of the second is still in progress, so timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb prize and with ion-clock work may influence the committee's view.
Redefinition of the second is not yet complete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect predicted by Kane and Mele in 2005 and observed by Molenkamp's group in HgTe wells in 2007 created the topological-insulator field, with a clear theory-and-experiment pairing and a large follow-up literature.
assessment.attribution: Kane-Mele provided the theory, and Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental demonstration, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal, which is not in the supplied credit. That omission is a serious attribution issue, and the three-person credit may not represent who did the original work.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in several materials, though some practical aims, such as dissipationless transport and topological quantum computing, are not realised; the 2016 prize covers related topological phase concepts, which may overlap.
uncertainties: Role of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and of Fu, Kane and Mele in 3D topological insulators is not in the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1992 discovery of 1992 QB1 provided the first direct observation of a trans-Neptunian object beyond Pluto and made the Kuiper belt an observed population, which reshaped the understanding of solar-system architecture. It is an original observational discovery with a clean, short experimental story.
assessment.attribution: Jewitt and Luu made the discovery using a CCD survey over several years, and the two-person credit is clean and also recognises a woman scientist. Earlier theoretical predictions (Edgeworth, Kuiper, Fernandez) are not credited, but the Nobel standard here is observational discovery.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by thousands of subsequent objects and by New Horizons; fully mature, though the field fits the physics prize only if the committee accepts astronomy-type discoveries.
uncertainties: Fit with the physics prize remit, as planetary science sits at the edge.
Precedence of theory and of Pluto-related lines of evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene (2011) and the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle created moire materials, a new platform with tunable correlations. Important and original, but I am conscious that it is still young.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental observation, so the credited names map directly onto the two decisive steps. Yuan Cao as first author of the experimental papers is not in the supplied credit, which I note as a procedural concern.
assessment.maturity: Replicated in many laboratories, yet the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still under active investigation, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Maturity: the interpretation of the correlated phases has not stabilised.
Yuan Cao and other early experimental contributors are not in the credited names.
